title: A CDC milestone is what most children do, counted as 75 percent or more
summary: The CDC says developmental milestones are things most children, 75 percent or more, can do by a certain age.
body: On its Learn the Signs pages, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says developmental milestones are things most children, 75 percent or more, can do by a certain age. Most, on these pages, is that fraction. The pages do not say every child. A child who does something later is not called ill by this sentence. The lists are the United States lists.

sources.title: Milestones by 9 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US CDC page, public domain. Updated and reviewed 16 May 2026. Supports the sentence that milestones are things most children (75% or more) can do by a certain age.
